security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation and contains no embedded executable code, prompt injection, or unauthorized network behavior. Seven findings are confirmed because documented workflows write database credentials to .env files; two additional medium-risk practices concern unpinned package execution and API keys in command arguments. All remaining static findings are Markdown or documentation-pattern false positives.

remediation.issue: Commands write database credentials to .env files.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must approve the target path, keep .env out of version control, and use restrictive file permissions before running these commands.

remediation.issue: Examples use npx with the latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Document tested version pins or require users to inspect and approve the package version before execution.

remediation.issue: API key examples place secrets in command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a secure environment variable, stdin, or an approved secret manager, and warn that command arguments can enter shell history and process listings.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned remote package execution
semantic_findings.description: Several setup commands use npx with the latest tag. A future package release can change what is executed, so users cannot reproduce or review the exact package version first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands explicitly use @latest. This is a real supply-chain and reproducibility concern, although the packages are named Prisma tooling.

semantic_findings.title: API key exposed in command arguments
semantic_findings.description: The non-interactive linking example places an API key directly in a command-line argument. Shell history and process inspection can expose that value.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both locations show the API key in a CLI argument. Command arguments are commonly recorded by shell history and can be visible to local processes.

content.value_statement: Prisma Postgres setup spans Console, command-line, and API workflows that can be difficult to compare. This skill provides focused guidance for provisioning databases, configuring connections, and building managed integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explain Console workflows for creating projects and viewing database data.
Guide temporary database provisioning with create-db and its documented flags.
Describe persistent database operations through the Prisma Platform CLI.
Explain local project linking and DATABASE_URL configuration.
Outline Management API service-token and OAuth workflows.
Show the Management API SDK setup pattern for typed integrations.
limitations: Does not execute commands, create databases, or access Prisma accounts.
Does not store, retrieve, or validate connection strings or API tokens.
Does not replace Prisma documentation for current API contracts or CLI flags.
Requires user approval before commands modify .env files or provision resources.

use_cases.title: Start a temporary development database
use_cases.description: Provision a short-lived Prisma Postgres database for a local prototype or preview environment.

use_cases.title: Connect an existing application
use_cases.description: Link a local Prisma project to an existing database and prepare its connection configuration.

use_cases.title: Build a provisioning integration
use_cases.description: Plan a service-token or OAuth workflow for creating and managing database resources programmatically.

prompt_templates.title: Create a development database
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the safest steps to create a temporary Prisma Postgres database for local development. Ask before running any command.

prompt_templates.title: Link a local project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me link my existing Prisma project to a Prisma Postgres database. Explain which files may change and do not expose secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an integration method
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Prisma Console, create-db, Platform CLI, and Management API for a production database workflow. Recommend one for my requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design OAuth provisioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure Prisma Management API OAuth integration. Include token storage, callback validation, least privilege, and secret-handling requirements.

output_examples.input: I need a temporary database for a local prototype.
output: Recommended workflow: use create-db for a short-lived development database.
Review the selected region and TTL before provisioning.
Do not commit the generated connection string or .env file.

output_examples.input: I need to connect an existing project to Prisma Postgres.
output: Use the project-linking workflow after confirming the target database.
The operation can update .env with DATABASE_URL.
Store the connection string securely and run Prisma commands only after review.

output_examples.input: My application provisions databases for customers.
output: Use the Management API for controlled programmatic provisioning.
Choose OAuth for user-delegated access or a service token for your own workspace.
Persist tokens securely and validate OAuth state and callback settings.

best_practices: Confirm the target project, database, and region before provisioning resources.
Keep connection strings and tokens in an approved secret store, not source control.
Pin and review CLI package versions before running remote package commands.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into shell commands or shared terminal logs.
Do not commit generated .env files or one-time connection URLs.
Do not use a service token with broader workspace access than the integration needs.

faq.question: Can this skill create a database for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only. You must review and approve any provisioning command.

faq.question: Which workflow is best for a quick prototype?
faq.answer: Use create-db for a temporary development database after reviewing its region, TTL, and output handling.

faq.question: When should I use the Management API?
faq.answer: Use it for controlled programmatic provisioning, backend automation, and multi-tenant workflows.

faq.question: Will linking modify my project?
faq.answer: It can update or create .env with DATABASE_URL. Review the file path and keep the file out of version control.

faq.question: How should I handle connection strings?
faq.answer: Treat them as secrets. Store them in an approved secret manager or protected environment configuration.

faq.question: Should I use an API key in a command argument?
faq.answer: Avoid it when possible. Command arguments may appear in shell history and process listings.
